candidate.blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — medication reconciliation and transition safety
candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — medication information at transitions
candidate.educational_objective: Maintain and communicate accurate medication information during discharge transitions.

options.A: Review the discharge medication information for accuracy and communicate the current medication list to the client and next care setting as applicable.
options.B: Copy the preadmission medication list without accounting for changes made during hospitalization.
options.C: Omit medication review when the admission was uncomplicated.
options.D: Assume medication information does not need to be communicated after discharge orders are written.

candidate.rationale: Joint Commission National Performance Goal #14 requires hospitals to maintain and communicate accurate patient medication information. At a transition such as discharge, medication information should reflect the current regimen and be communicated appropriately rather than simply copying an outdated preadmission list. A is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Hospitals must maintain and communicate accurate patient medication information as part of medication safety.
candidate.source_document_title: National Performance Goal #14: Effectively Managing Medications
candidate.source_locator: Standards — hospital maintains and communicates accurate patient medication information
candidate.stem: At discharge, which action best supports accurate medication information during the transition of care?
